messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

Customers should also be able to email support and reply from their mail client. Add this with
Action Mailbox. Each business receives mail at its subdomain under `HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN`,
default `support.example.test`; Acme gets `acme@support.example.test`.

Use Action Mailbox's relay ingress at `/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails`, authenticated
with `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD`. In test, process incoming mail before the request completes
so a separate worker isn't needed.

Incoming mail should open a ticket with its subject and plain-text message.

Find the business from the recipients, including Cc. Ignore mail addressed to multiple businesses.
Reuse an existing customer, or create one and send a verification email so they can later use the portal.
Receiving email shouldn't verify their account.

When staff post a public reply to an email-origin ticket, email it to the requester. Give each
ticket a private reply address at the support domain, so the customer's next email returns to
the right conversation. Only the requester may reply by email. Replies reopen pending or solved
tickets; a new message to the plain support address opens a new ticket.

Deduplicate deliveries by Message-ID. Invalid deliveries must not block a later valid retry.
Ignore automated/list mail.

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "digest"
require "securerandom"

module TokenDigestable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  class_methods do
    def generate_raw_token
      SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32, padding: false)
    end

    def digest_token(raw_token)
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw_token.to_s)
    end

    def find_by_raw_token(raw_token)
      return nil if raw_token.blank?

      find_by(token_digest: digest_token(raw_token))
    end
  end
end

class AccountMailer < ApplicationMailer
  def email_verification(user, raw_token)
    @user = user
    @account = user.account
    @verification_url = HelpdeskConfig.verify_email_url(account: @account, token: raw_token)

    message = mail(

      subject: "Verify your email for #{@account.name}"

require "digest"
require "securerandom"

module TokenDigestable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  class_methods do
    def generate_raw_token
      SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32, padding: false)
    end

    def digest_token(raw_token)
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw_token.to_s)
    end

    def find_by_raw_token(raw_token)
      return nil if raw_token.blank?

      find_by(token_digest: digest_token(raw_token))
    end
  end
end

class User < ApplicationRecord

  has_many :email_verifications, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :password_resets, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :requested_tickets, class_name: "Ticket", foreign_key: :requester_id, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :requester
  has_many :assigned_tickets, class_name: "Ticket", foreign_key: :assignee_id, dependent: :nullify, validate: false, inverse_of: :assignee
  has_many :ticket_comments, foreign_key: :author_id, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :author
  has_many :sent_invitations, class_name: "Invitation", foreign_key: :invited_by_id, dependent: :nullify, inverse_of: :invited_by

  normalizes :name, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :email, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }
  validates :email,
    presence: true,
    length: { maximum: 255 },
    format: { with: EMAIL_FORMAT },
    uniqueness: { scope: :account_id, case_sensitive: false }
  validates :role, presence: true, inclusion: { in: ROLES }
  validates :password, length: { minimum: MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH }, if: -> { password.present? }

  scope :ordered_by_id, -> { order(id: :asc) }
  scope :admins, -> { where(role: "admin") }
  scope :agents, -> { where(role: "agent") }
  scope :customers, -> { where(role: "customer") }
  scope :staff, -> { where(role: %w[admin agent]) }
  scope :active, -> { where(suspended_at: nil) }
  scope :suspended, -> { where.not(suspended_at: nil) }

  def verified?
    email_verified_at.present?
  end

  def suspended?
    suspended_at.present?
  end

  def active?
    !suspended?
  end

  def owner?
    account.owner_id == id
  end

  def admin?
    role == "admin"
  end

  def agent?
    role == "agent"
  end

  def customer?
    role == "customer"
  end

  def staff?
    admin? || agent?
  end

  def revoke_sessions!
    sessions.delete_all
  end

  def verify_email!
    transaction do
      update!(email_verified_at: Time.current) unless verified?
      email_verifications.delete_all
    end

    transaction do
      now = Time.current

      save!
      revoke_sessions!
      assigned_tickets.update_all(assignee_id: nil, updated_at: now)
    end
  end

  def unsuspend!
    update!(suspended_at: nil)

class PasswordReset < ApplicationRecord
  include TokenDigestable

  EXPIRY = 2.hours

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :user

  validates :token_digest, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :expires_at, presence: true

  scope :active, -> { where("expires_at > ?", Time.current) }

  attr_accessor :raw_token

  def self.issue_for(user)
    raw = generate_raw_token
    reset = nil
    transaction do
      user.password_resets.delete_all
      reset = create!(
        account: user.account,
        user: user,
        token_digest: digest_token(raw),
        expires_at: EXPIRY.from_now
      )
    end
    reset.raw_token = raw
    reset
  end
end

require_relative "../config/environment"
require "rails/test_help"

require "uri"

module ActiveSupport
  class TestCase
    setup do
      ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    end

    def with_env(overrides)
      originals = {}
      overrides.each do |key, value|
        key_s = key.to_s
        originals[key_s] = ENV.key?(key_s) ? ENV[key_s] : :__unset__
        if value.nil?
          ENV.delete(key_s)
        else
          ENV[key_s] = value
        end
      end
      yield
    ensure
      originals.each do |key_s, original|
        if original == :__unset__
          ENV.delete(key_s)
        else
          ENV[key_s] = original
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

module ApiTestHelper
  def json_body
    JSON.parse(response.body)
  end

  def account_headers(subdomain, token: nil, extra: {})
    headers = {
      "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain,
      "Accept" => "application/json"
    }
    headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer #{token}" if token
    headers.merge(extra)
  end

  def extract_link_from_mail(mail, path:)
    body = mail.body.decoded
    match = body.match(%r{https?://[^\s]+#{Regexp.escape(path)}\?[^\s]+})
    assert_not_nil match, "Expected link containing #{path} in mail body:\n#{body}"
    match[0]
  end

  def extract_query_params(url)
    uri = URI.parse(url)
    URI.decode_www_form(uri.query.to_s).to_h
  end

  def create_account_via_api(name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    post "/api/v1/account/create",
      params: {
        account: {
          name: name,
          subdomain: subdomain,
          admin: {
            name: admin_name,
            email: email,
            password: password
          }
        }
      },
      as: :json
  end

  def register_customer_via_api(subdomain: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password")
    post "/api/v1/registrations",
      params: {
        user: {
          name: name,
          email: email,
          password: password
        }
      },
      headers: account_headers(subdomain),
      as: :json
  end

  def verify_last_email!(subdomain:)
    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
    assert_not_nil mail, "Expected a verification email to have been sent"
    link = extract_link_from_mail(mail, path: "/verify-email")
    params = extract_query_params(link)
    post "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm",
      params: { email_verification: { token: params["token"] } },
      headers: account_headers(subdomain),
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    params["token"]
  end

  def sign_in_via_api(subdomain:, email:, password:)
    post "/api/v1/sessions",
      params: { session: { email: email, password: password } },
      headers: account_headers(subdomain),
      as: :json
    assert_response :created
    json_body.dig("session", "token")
  end

  def invite_staff_via_api(subdomain: "acme", token:, email:, role: "agent")
    post "/api/v1/invitations",
      params: { invitation: { email: email, role: role } },
      headers: account_headers(subdomain, token: token),
      as: :json
  end

  def extract_last_invitation_token
    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
    assert_not_nil mail, "Expected an invitation email to have been sent"
    link = extract_link_from_mail(mail, path: "/accept-invitation")
    extract_query_params(link)["token"]
  end

  def accept_invitation_via_api(subdomain: "acme", token:, name:, password:)

        invitation_acceptance: {
          token: token,
          name: name,
          password: password
        }
      },
      headers: account_headers(subdomain),
      as: :json
  end

module ActionMailbox
  # Ingests inbound emails relayed from an SMTP server.
  #
  # Authenticates requests using HTTP basic access authentication. The username is always +actionmailbox+, and the
  # password is read from the application's encrypted credentials or an environment variable. See the Usage section below.
  #
  # Note that basic authentication is insecure over unencrypted HTTP. An attacker that intercepts cleartext requests to
  # the ingress can learn its password. You should only use this ingress over HTTPS.
  #
  # Returns:
  #
  # - <tt>204 No Content</tt> if an inbound email is successfully recorded and enqueued for routing to the appropriate mailbox
  # - <tt>401 Unauthorized</tt> if the request could not be authenticated
  # - <tt>404 Not Found</tt> if Action Mailbox is not configured to accept inbound emails relayed from an SMTP server
  # - <tt>415 Unsupported Media Type</tt> if the request does not contain an RFC 822 message
  # - <tt>500 Server Error</tt> if the ingress password is not configured, or if one of the Active Record database,
  #   the Active Storage service, or the Active Job backend is misconfigured or unavailable
  #
  # == Usage
  #
  # 1. Tell Action Mailbox to accept emails from an SMTP relay:
  #
  #        # config/environments/production.rb
  #        config.action_mailbox.ingress = :relay
  #
  # 2. Generate a strong password that Action Mailbox can use to authenticate requests to the ingress.
  #
  #    Use <tt>bin/rails credentials:edit</tt> to add the password to your application's encrypted credentials under
  #    +action_mailbox.ingress_password+, where Action Mailbox will automatically find it:
  #
  #        action_mailbox:
  #          ingress_password: ...
  #

  # by an Action Mailer method, like so:

  #     before_processing :ensure_sender_is_a_user
  #

  #       def ensure_sender_is_a_user

  # complete, the status is changed to +delivered+. If a bounce is triggered, then +bounced+. If an unhandled
  # exception is bubbled up, then +failed+.

    end

      inbound_email.bounced!
      message.deliver_later
    end

    # Immediately sends the given +message+ and changes the inbound email's status to +:bounced+.

        job.dup.tap do |new_job|
          new_job[:at] = Time.at(new_job[:at]) if new_job[:at]
          new_job[:args] = ActiveJob::Arguments.deserialize(new_job[:args]) if new_job[:args]
        end
      end

      def instantiate_job(payload, skip_deserialize_arguments: false)
        job = payload[:job].deserialize(payload)
        job.scheduled_at = Time.at(payload[:at]) if payload.key?(:at)
        job.send(:deserialize_arguments_if_needed) unless skip_deserialize_arguments
        job
      end

      def queue_adapter_changed_jobs
        (ActiveJob::Base.descendants << ActiveJob::Base).select do |klass|
          # only override explicitly set adapters, a quirk of `class_attribute`
          klass.singleton_class.public_instance_methods(false).include?(:_queue_adapter)
        end
      end

      def validate_option(only: nil, except: nil)
        raise ArgumentError, "Cannot specify both `:only` and `:except` options." if only && except
      end
  end
end

**Deep Dive into Action Mailbox and Active Job Configuration**

Okay, let's break this down systematically. I'm focusing on how `ActiveJob` and `ActionMailbox` interact, especially when testing, and how this relates to our application's configuration.

First, I need to understand how the test environment handles queued jobs. I see that `ActiveJob::TestHelper`'s `before_setup` method is crucial. When `config.active_job.queue_adapter = :inline` is set, `ActiveJob` retains the `InlineAdapter`. This is the crux of the immediate execution we're seeing in tests.

Now, let's connect this to `ActionMailbox::InboundEmail::Routable`. The `after_create_commit :route_later` callback is key. When an inbound email is created, it enqueues a `RoutingJob` *later* (which, with `:inline`, means immediately). But, *wait*, what does `after_create_commit` *really* mean in the context of integration tests and transactions? In Rails 8.1, this means it executes after the inner transaction within the `create!` finishes, a savepoint is released or the transaction stack completes, and `after_commit` is triggered.

Consider this: if we run Puma in a test environment (e.g., using an external HTTP test runner), a `create!` will commit the transaction. That triggers the `after_create_commit` callback, which queues the `ActionMailbox::RoutingJob` for *immediate* execution via the `:inline` adapter. This then executes *right before* the HTTP response (likely a `204 No Content`) is sent.

So here's the critical question: What happens if `ActionMailbox::RoutingJob` raises an unhandled exception when using `:inline`? The response would become a 500. This could be useful during debugging, but it also necessitates that the mailbox itself *must* handle all expected invalid or ignored cases cleanly (bounced emails, etc.) to prevent unhandled exceptions.

Let's also remember `IncinerationJob` and its config. In a typical test setup, we'd have `config.active_job.queue_adapter = :inline` and `config.action_mailbox.incinerate = false`. But what about development or production, where a queue adapter is *usually* used? ActiveJob defaults to `:async`, which *does* support `enqueue_at`. This is important for jobs that need to be scheduled for later execution.

Now, let's address the prompt about using Action Mailbox's relay ingress, especially in test environments. The prompt specifies processing incoming mail *before* the request completes in the test environment. In this scenario, we set `config.action_mailbox.ingress = :relay` in `config/application.rb` (which applies to *all* environments). Then in `config/environments/test.rb` we set `config.active_job.queue_adapter = :inline` and `config.action_mailbox.incinerate = false`

Finally, I need to check how Active Storage is configured, since Action Mailbox depends on it (specifically the `has_one_attached :raw_email` relationship). I'll go through the `config/storage.yml` file and `config.active_storage.service` across all environments (`development.rb`, `test.rb`, `production.rb`) to make sure everything's set up correctly. *   `config/storage.yml`: `test`, `local` configurations

messages.thinking:
**In-Depth Analysis of Action Mailbox and Email Ingress**

Okay, so I've been digging deep into how Action Mailbox works and how to best implement the email ingress system for this project. I've got a pretty solid grasp on how it's all going to work, and I'm ready to roll up my sleeves and get this built in a way that is robust, deduplicates well, and most importantly doesn't break at any given time.

My initial thought was that the `credentials.yml.enc` file wasn't setting the `action_mailbox.ingress_password`, which meant the system was grabbing it dynamically from the `ENV` variable on every request, which is what I wanted.

But then I had to go back and check. I needed to see how the system would authenticate and handle the case where that `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD` isn't set. If the password isn't there and someone hits the mail route, we get a 500 error, which is the documented Action Mailbox behavior. However, with the password set, it uses basic auth.

The other thing to check was whether `ActionMailbox::BaseController` still inherits from `ActionController::Base` even in an API-only Rails app. The answer is yes, so `http_basic_authenticate_or_request_with` is still in play, and so is testing the `/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails` route in integration tests.

Now, let's start at the beginning and go through the requirements with extreme detail.

### Requirement 1: Support Domain & Business Email Addressing

This is where things start getting interesting. The plan is to create support addresses for each business using a subdomain. I added `support_domain` to `HelpdeskConfig` and `support_address_for(account)` to create those addresses. I've got some ideas on how to normalize the email addresses, which I think is a good idea. I think strip white space, downcase, and then strip the `@` if it accidentally shows up at the beginning.

### Requirement 2: Relay Ingress & Test Mode Processing

I verified the configuration steps for Action Mailbox (enabling engines, setting the ingress to relay, adding migrations, setting up storage) and have a strong understanding of how the email will come into the application.

Then, I focused on the test environment. Specifically, I'm working through how to make sure that "Invalid deliveries must not block a later valid retry" will work. I reviewed the code for `Relay::InboundEmailsController#create` and, most importantly, `ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.create_and_extract_message_id!` because that has the unique index that will handle deduplication.

This is where it gets complex. The index uses `message_id` and `message_checksum`. If the raw bytes are identical (`message_id` and `message_checksum` are the same), it’s easy to deduplicate. But what if the `message_id` is the same, but the bytes are different (different headers, minor changes, etc.)?

I really need to figure out how to make sure we don't block valid retries of emails, but also how to ensure that duplicate emails don't cause problems in the system. The challenge is that an invalid email now could have a valid email at a later time.

The thing that came to mind was deduplication. I'll need to think about that very carefully.

I think the best solution is a nullable column in `ticket_comments` called `inbound_message_id`. By creating a unique partial index on that column, I can ensure that a valid inbound email creates **exactly one** `TicketComment` (either the initial comment of a new ticket or a reply to an existing ticket). If an email is invalid (wrong recipient, multiple recipients, etc.), no `TicketComment` is created, so the system is not blocked.

Now, that means that if an email *is* valid, it gets recorded in the database and then, in case of a racing condition, the unique index guarantees that only ONE gets saved. If a record is not unique, it will be skipped by the database.

I considered what happens if the account is deleted and the comment is deleted too. No problem because, with a cascade delete, that covers all the bases.

### Other Considerations

Now I need to consider where I should store processed `Message-ID`s, the scope of deduplication, and how to handle emails without `Message-ID`s. I also need to think about case sensitivity and concurrency. Also what to do with messages that are bounced, vs delivered.

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing Message-ID Handling in Action Mailbox**

Okay, so I've been digging into how we're handling `Message-ID` within the context of `Action Mailbox` and its interaction with the `Mail` gem. Here's what I've found, and the implications I'm seeing:

First, `Mail` itself is doing some cleanup. It strips the angle brackets (`<` and `>`) from the `message_id` and, of course, gives us `nil` if there's no `Message-ID` header. This is the starting point. But `Mail` behaves oddly: If the header is blank (e.g., `Message-ID: `), it *generates* a random ID, but `mail.header[:message_id]&.unparsed_value` will be `nil`.

Now, the core of the problem: when the `Message-ID` header is *missing* entirely, `mail.message_id` returns `nil`. That means we have to consider what should happen. `ActionMailbox` generates a `message_id` based on the message checksum if no header exists.

Here's the critical question: When there's no `Message-ID` header at all, do we use the checksum-based `inbound_email.message_id` (so we still deduplicate based on raw message content), or do we let `inbound_message_id` remain `nil`, effectively allowing the *same* email (identical raw bytes) sent twice without an ID to create two tickets? I lean towards keeping the nil, so we can track the same email arriving twice without a header.

Here's the scenario: Imagine a customer sends an email without a `Message-ID` and Action Mailbox generates `<sha1_checksum@hostname.mail>`.

*   If the same email (identical bytes) comes twice without a `Message-ID`, the checksum is the same, so `inbound_email` deduplicates it.
*   If *two different* emails arrive without a `Message-ID` (say, two test emails), the checksums will be different, creating distinct `inbound_email.message_id` values (or `nil`), so we have two unique tickets.
*   If an email *does* have a `Message-ID`, `mail.message_id` gives us a clean value.

Now, let's consider case-sensitivity. RFC 5322 says the part *before* the `@` is case-sensitive, but the domain (after the `@`) is usually case-insensitive. Practically, many deduplicators normalize, and there's cleaning up to do anyway, like removing `<` `>`, and whitespace.

What happens if someone sends `<MSG-1@Example.Test>` and then retries with `<msg-1@example.test>`? I need to test that. Could two *different* emails have `Message-ID`s differing *only* in case? Extremely rare in practice! Even if it *could* happen because of `id-left` being base64-like, the chance of collisions is negligible.

So, I'm thinking of normalizing `Message-ID` in the following way:

1.  Strip whitespace from the raw ID.
2.  Remove `<` and `>` if present.
3.  Lowercase the *domain* part after the `@`.

But I have to be careful here! I need to ensure existing tests that check our ID cleanup still work! Does someone explicitly send `<ABC@example.test>` and `<abc@example.test>` to test case-insensitive matching? Probably not! It’s more likely that existing tests check for normalization of whitespace and brackets.

The question then becomes: What is `ActionMailbox::InboundEmail` *itself* storing? It’s directly storing `Mail.from_source(source).message_id`, which already strips the brackets and whitespace and preserves case.

Finally, what happens if the `Message-ID` header has something `Mail` can't parse? We get `nil` from `mail.message_id`, even though `mail.header[:message_id]` has something in it. I need to test that edge case (`Message-ID: custom-id-without-at` and `<custom-id-without-at>`).

messages.thinking:
**Deduplication and Recipient Resolution: A Deep Dive**

Okay, so I've been thinking about the incoming mail and how to handle it, particularly around deduplication and business resolution. The `mail` library seems to handle the `<custom-id-without-at>` and `Message-Id:` headers nicely, which is a good starting point. My initial thought was about the scope of `inbound_message_id` for deduplication: should it be global or per-account? Given that RFC 5322 dictates that `Message-ID` is globally unique, that seems to make the most sense. However, I had to consider edge cases, like a single email potentially being delivered to multiple businesses via separate SMTP envelopes (like with BCC).

Even if a single email gets delivered to two businesses, or even if an invalid delivery went to one business while another was valid, the `inbound_message_id` being unique across the system handles that properly. The key is to avoid accidentally double-processing, even with different delivery outcomes. I need to make sure I catch the cases where a single email arrives multiple times. I'd hate to create duplicate tickets.

I considered a test case where someone might send a valid email with a `Message-ID` to one business and then another email with the same `Message-ID` to another business, but it seems unlikely. A Message-ID should uniquely identify *one* email. This led me to conclude that a globally unique `inbound_message_id` is the right approach. It aligns with Action Mailbox's concept of a global `message_id` and addresses the "Deduplicate deliveries by Message-ID" requirement perfectly.

The edge case with BCC and separate deliveries is also handled by global deduplication. Action Mailbox also uses a global `message_id` so this makes sense. So, for normalization of `Message-ID`, I can extract the value using `mail.header[:message_id]&.unparsed_value.present?` and then `mail.message_id.to_s.strip` and strip surrounding `<` and `>` characters if any, making sure to avoid truncation with a text or string column of appropriate length, and verifying the `db/schema.rb` file. messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive into the Design Philosophy: Email Handling and Customer Lifecycle**

Okay, wow, reading through these tests is incredibly enlightening! The design principles of this system are becoming crystal clear. It's incredibly thorough and security-conscious, with a laser focus on multi-tenancy and robust account management.

My mind is racing as I'm thinking through all of these scenarios. They're all very sensible, for example: strictly enforcing multi-tenancy, rejecting activity from cancelled or suspended accounts, and the rigorous email verification process – it's all solid. The unverified user restrictions are particularly well-thought-out. The password reset flow is also good.

Now, let's trace this entire customer flow that relies on email creation.
1.  A new customer sends an email.
2.  Upon receipt, a new user is created in the database:
    *   The system uses the email address, normalizes it, and extracts the customer's name. A random password is automatically generated.
    *   Crucially, this new user is *not* immediately verified.
3.  An email verification token is issued and sent via mailer.
4.  Only after verification via the email link, can the user log in.

What about *existing* customers? Let's consider those scenarios:

*   For an existing *verified* customer: Re-use the existing user; no new verification email.
*   For an existing *unverified* customer: The user is re-used, and no new verification email is sent. It's only sent for *new* customer creation.
*   For an existing *staff* user: The existing staff user is used, there is no verification.
*   For a sender with a *pending staff invitation*: This email should be rejected or handled specially to prevent conflicts with the invitation process.
*   For a sender that is a customer in *another* account: A new user is created in *this* account, and this account's verification email is sent.

One more thing! The system needs to be carefully designed to avoid conflicts during the creation of new customers, if there are multiple incoming emails simultaneously.

Let's carefully examine **Plain-Text Body Extraction**!
The requirements for the system indicate that it should be able to process all of the following:
*   Standard text/plain emails with or without charset specifications and various transfer encodings.
*   Multipart/alternative emails, always extracting the `text/plain` part *only*.
*   Multipart/mixed emails with both plain text and attachments. The system needs to be careful not to extract the contents of file attachments.
*   **Crucially**: emails that are *only* in HTML format. We must test whether HTML content is correctly handled. Should the system simply strip the HTML tags or reject the email entirely? The choice here is important, and tests need to cover both scenarios.

messages.thinking:
**Decoding Email Body Logic** Okay, this is exciting! I've made some breakthroughs looking at Results #4 and #6! It looks like the `mail` gem's `text_part` is already doing the right thing with attachments, which is great – it ignores them. Even better, when traversing parts, we explicitly filter them. In Result #6, I saw that `m6.body.decoded` returns `"Caf\xE9\r\n"` with `ASCII-8BIT` encoding and a charset of `"ISO-8859-1"`. If I pass the raw, encoded string to PostgreSQL, it, or Ruby, will probably choke on those invalid UTF-8 bytes! I need to *decode* using the part's charset. I'm going to create a `decode_part_text` method. It will handle the decoding, converting to UTF-8, replacing invalid characters, stripping null bytes (`\x00`), normalizing line endings (`\r\n` to `\n`), and stripping whitespace. I should test it on that ISO-8859-1 string to make sure it becomes `"Café"` in UTF-8! Now, the really critical bit: HTML-only emails. I need to be *very* careful here, looking at Results #4 and #5. What if an email has no `text/plain` part, just a `text/html` part? I'm thinking: * **Case A:** If there's a `text/plain` part (either standalone or within a `multipart/*` structure), use it. Simple! * **Case B:** **NO** `text/plain` part, *only* `text/html`. This is where I need to think hard. Should I: 1. Convert the HTML to plain text? Maybe using Nokogiri or `Rails::Html::FullSanitizer`, then decoding HTML entities, and preserving block/line breaks? 2. Reject HTML-only emails as invalid? Re-reading the prompt, it says incoming mail should open a ticket with subject and *plain-text* message. Let's imagine: * If an email has both `text/plain` and `text/html`, both options extract the `text/plain`! * But, if the email is HTML-only, should I reject it? No way! Real helpdesks (Zendesk, Help Scout, etc.) handle HTML-only emails all the time. They convert the HTML to clean plain text. If the HTML is *just* tags and whitespace (e.g., `
`), the resulting text will be blank, and it will be rejected as empty body! If the email has, for example, a PDF attachment only, there will be no plain text, and it's also rejected as blank. So, I will need to use Option 1! Finally, let's check if Nokogiri, Loofah, or rails-html-sanitizer is already installed in the Gemfile.lock. We might save some time!

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing Email Processing for Ticket Creation**

Okay, first things first: `nokogiri` and `loofah` are already available, bundled with Rails – good. Now, when converting HTML to plain text, if there's no `text/plain` part, `nokogiri` is going to make this pretty straightforward: remove the cruft, replace line breaks and block elements with proper spacing, extract the text, and clean up the whitespace. Really clean extraction using `.text` is a lifesaver with HTML entity decoding. And if `text/plain` *does* exist, use it directly – with character set decoding and normalization.

But... a multipart email with a *blank* `text/plain` part alongside actual `text/html` content needs careful handling. If `text/plain` is just whitespace, fall back to the HTML conversion. If *that* ends up blank too, we reject it as an empty message. That's the correct approach. Let's make sure that is considered.

Now, let's circle back to this blank subject issue. This is crucial. What if an incoming email, meant to start a *new* ticket, has no subject line?

Option A: Fall back to `"(No subject)"`.
Option B: Reject and ignore.

Which is correct? Let's check:

1.  "Incoming mail should open a ticket with its subject and plain-text message."
2.  Deduplicate by `Message-ID`. Invalid deliveries mustn't block valid retries.
3.  Invalid deliveries: multiple businesses, automated mail, missing/invalid `From`, blank body, invalid reply token, unauthorized sender, suspended sender.

The prompt *never* says to ignore emails without a subject! Plus, `Ticket` validates presence AND length for `subject`. So, is it `validates :subject, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }`? The RFC says `Subject` is optional. Real helpdesk systems default to `"(No subject)"` rather than losing a customer's email. A missing or blank body creates a missing or blank comment, which also isn't acceptable.

Now, consider test cases for invalid deliveries! The prompt explicitly says invalid deliveries, so we need to think this through. Multiple businesses, automated mail, and so on... these are all *unambiguously* invalid. *Missing* subject for a real customer email is different.

Falling back to `"(No subject)"` when `mail.subject` is empty aligns with standard helpdesk behavior and handles RFC 5322 subject-less emails gracefully. Any email *with* a subject uses that subject. Any email *without* one defaults to `"(No subject)"` – so no silently dropped emails! Any subject over 255 chars is truncated, so we don't crash. Empty/whitespace bodies ARE rejected, as they should be!

Finally, whitespace normalization of subjects: `" Cannot log in "` becomes `"Cannot log in"`, folded headers become single lines, and encoded subjects get decoded. The existing code handles this. Let's run a quick test with Ruby `Mail` to be certain.

*   **Account and Ticket Verification:** We are looking up the account 'acme', ensuring it exists and is active. We'll grab the ticket by `email_reply_token`, scoped to that account. We make sure that `ticket.account_id == account.id` is exactly the same, using either a constant-time comparison or an exact indexed lookup.
*   **Recipient Integrity:** We double-check that no other business or ticket reply address is addressed in any other recipient.
*   **Requester Authentication:** The reply MUST be from the ticket's requester, so we're comparing `sender_email == ticket.requester.email` (lowercased), and rejecting any email that is not the requester's. We also need to bounce the email if the requester is suspended. If the ticket requester is unverified, their email reply should still be allowed, so that they can reply to the initial email.
*   **Pending/Solved Ticket Reopening:** We must mirror the exact behavior in `RequestsController#update` which uses `open` status for pending or solved tickets. We have to check if the status of a pending or solved ticket changes to open. We use transactions to ensure all changes happen atomically, including changes to `updated_at` and `public_updated_at` upon `ticket.save!`. We make sure to note that the reply must not alter the `ticket.priority` or `ticket.assignee_id`.
*   **New Ticket Creation:** A new email to `acme@support.example.test` MUST open a **NEW** ticket, even if the customer has an open ticket.
*   **Reply-All Edge Case:** If an email is sent to `acme+<valid_token>@support.example.test` and also `acme@support.example.test`, but the sender is not the requester, it MUST be rejected. We cannot allow unauthorized senders to hijack the reply thread, nor can we fall back to opening a new ticket.

1.  **RFC 3834 – `Auto-Submitted`:** If this header is present, and its value is NOT `"no"`, we ignore it. `"no"` implies a human-sent email.
2.  **RFC 2076 / RFC 3834 – `Precedence`:** We ignore emails with `Precedence` values like `bulk`, `junk`, `list`, `auto_reply`, or similar.
3.  **RFC 2919 / RFC 2369 – Mailing List Headers:** If we have the presence of `List-Id`, `List-Unsubscribe`, and any of the other List headers, then we will ignore it.

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "uri"

module HelpdeskConfig
  DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL = "http://localhost:3001"
  DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM = "support@example.test"
  DEFAULT_SUPPORT_DOMAIN = "support.example.test"

  module_function

  def frontend_url
    raw = ENV["HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL"].to_s.strip
    url = raw.empty? ? DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL : raw
    url.sub(%r{/+\z}, "")
  end

  def frontend_origin
    normalize_origin(frontend_url, allow_path: true)
  end

  def allowed_origin?(origin)
    expected = frontend_origin
    actual = normalize_origin(origin, allow_path: false)
    expected.present? && actual.present? && actual == expected
  end

  def mail_from
    raw = ENV["HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM"].to_s.strip
    raw.empty? ? DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM : raw
  end

  def support_domain
    raw = ENV["HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN"].to_s.strip.downcase
    raw = raw.delete_prefix("@")
    raw.empty? ? DEFAULT_SUPPORT_DOMAIN : raw
  end

  def support_address_for(account)
    "#{account.subdomain}@#{support_domain}"
  end

  def ticket_reply_address(ticket)
    return nil if ticket.email_reply_token.blank?

    "#{ticket.account.subdomain}+#{ticket.email_reply_token}@#{support_domain}"
  end

  def verify_email_url(account:, token:)
    query = URI.encode_www_form(account: account.subdomain, token: token)
    "#{frontend_url}/verify-email?#{query}"
  end

  def reset_password_url(account:, token:)
    query = URI.encode_www_form(account: account.subdomain, token: token)
    "#{frontend_url}/reset-password?#{query}"
  end

  def accept_invitation_url(account:, token:)
    query = URI.encode_www_form(account: account.subdomain, token: token)
    "#{frontend_url}/accept-invitation?#{query}"
  end

  def normalize_origin(value, allow_path:)
    return nil if value.blank?

    uri = URI.parse(value.to_s.strip)
    return nil unless uri.scheme && uri.host
    return nil if uri.userinfo.present?

    unless allow_path
      return nil unless uri.path.blank? && uri.query.nil? && uri.fragment.nil?
    end

    scheme = uri.scheme.downcase
    return nil unless %w[http https].include?(scheme)

    host = uri.host.downcase
    default_port = (scheme == "https" ? 443 : 80)
    port_part = (uri.port && uri.port != default_port) ? ":#{uri.port}" : ""
    "#{scheme}://#{host}#{port_part}"
  rescue URI::InvalidURIError
    nil
  end
end
EOF

I'll need a way to generate that token; `generate_email_reply_token` will use `SecureRandom.hex(16)`. That's 128 bits of entropy, which is more than sufficient. I also want a handy method, `email_reply_address`, that returns the correct reply address based on whether it's an email origin and the presence of the token. Finally, since it's an ActiveRecord boolean, I'll leverage the existing `email_origin?` method.

I've already defined `validates :inbound_message_id, uniqueness: true, allow_nil: true`. That covers the bases. Duplicate inbound message checks are already being done in the `SupportMailbox` and model validations should catch duplicates during tests, so that is perfect. Also, the DB unique partial index should catch concurrent race conditions. Hold on...the `allow_nil: true` means we're *skipping* the uniqueness check when `inbound_message_id` is nil (portal comments, staff comments, emails without Message-ID). That's perfect. But, let's normalize this field. A blank string passed in could be problematic. # frozen_string_literal: true

require "securerandom"

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true, inverse_of: :assigned_tickets

  has_many :comments, class_name: "TicketComment", dependent: :delete_all, inverse_of: :ticket

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }

  before_validation :ensure_email_reply_token, if: :email_origin?

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :priority, presence: true, inclusion: { in: PRIORITIES }
  validates :email_reply_token, presence: true, uniqueness: true, if: :email_origin?
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_is_active_staff_in_account, if: -> { assignee_id.present? && (new_record? || will_save_change_to_assignee_id?) }

  before_create :initialize_public_updated_at
  before_update :sync_public_updated_at

  scope :recently_active_first, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :recently_publicly_active_first, -> { order(public_updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :with_status, ->(status) { where(status: status) }
  scope :with_priority, ->(priority) { where(priority: priority) }
  scope :unassigned, -> { where(assignee_id: nil) }
  scope :assigned_to, ->(assignee_id) { where(assignee_id: assignee_id) }
  scope :requested_by, ->(requester_id) { where(requester_id: requester_id) }

  def self.generate_email_reply_token
    SecureRandom.hex(16)
  end

  def self.search_text(query)
    raw = query.to_s
    return none unless raw.valid_encoding?

    term = raw.strip
    return all if term.empty?
    return none if term.include?("\x00")

    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(term)}%"
    where(
      <<~'SQL'.squish,
        tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\'
        OR EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM ticket_comments
          WHERE ticket_comments.ticket_id = tickets.id
            AND ticket_comments.account_id = tickets.account_id
            AND ticket_comments.public = TRUE
            AND ticket_comments.body ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\'
        )
      SQL
      pattern: pattern
    )
  end

  def open?
    status == "open"
  end

  def pending?
    status == "pending"
  end

  def solved?
    status == "solved"
  end

  def normal_priority?
    priority == "normal"
  end

  def high_priority?
    priority == "high"
  end

  def email_reply_address
    return nil unless email_origin? && email_reply_token.present?

    HelpdeskConfig.ticket_reply_address(self)
  end

  private

  def ensure_email_reply_token
    self.email_reply_token ||= self.class.generate_email_reply_token
  end

  def initialize_public_updated_at
    now = Time.current
    self.created_at ||= now
    self.updated_at ||= now
    self.public_updated_at ||= updated_at
  end

  def sync_public_updated_at
    return unless will_save_change_to_status? || will_save_change_to_subject?

    now = Time.current
    self.updated_at = now
    self.public_updated_at = now
  end

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    return unless requester && account_id

    if requester.account_id != account_id
      errors.add(:requester, "must belong to the same account")
    end
  end

  def assignee_is_active_staff_in_account
    return if assignee_id.nil?

    if assignee.nil? || assignee.account_id != account_id || !assignee.staff? || assignee.suspended?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member in this account")
    end
  end
end
EOF

# frozen_string_literal: true

class TicketComment < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :ticket, inverse_of: :comments
  belongs_to :author, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :ticket_comments

  attr_accessor :skip_ticket_touch

  normalizes :inbound_message_id, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.presence }

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :public, inclusion: { in: [ true, false ] }
  validates :inbound_message_id, uniqueness: true, allow_nil: true
  validate :associations_belong_to_account

  after_create :touch_ticket, unless: :skip_ticket_touch

  scope :public_only, -> { where(public: true) }
  scope :oldest_first, -> { order(created_at: :asc, id: :asc) }

  private

  def touch_ticket
    return unless ticket&.persisted?

    now = Time.current
    if public?
      ticket.update_columns(updated_at: now, public_updated_at: now)
    else
      ticket.update_columns(updated_at: now)
    end
  end

  def associations_belong_to_account
    return unless account_id

    if ticket && ticket.account_id != account_id
      errors.add(:ticket, "must belong to the same account")
    end

    if author && author.account_id != account_id
      errors.add(:author, "must belong to the same account")
    end
  end
end

mkdir -p app/views/ticket_mailer

cat <<'EOF' > app/mailers/ticket_mailer.rb
# frozen_string_literal: true

class TicketMailer < ApplicationMailer
  SAFE_MESSAGE_ID_FORMAT = /\A[^\s<>]+\z/

  def staff_reply(ticket, comment)
    @ticket = ticket
    @comment = comment
    @account = ticket.account
    @requester = ticket.requester
    @author = comment.author

    reply_address = @ticket.email_reply_address
    subject_line = @ticket.subject.match?(/\Are:/i) ? @ticket.subject : "Re: #{@ticket.subject}"

    references = build_references(@ticket)
    if references.any?
      headers["In-Reply-To"] = references.last
      headers["References"] = references.join(" ")
    end

    message = mail(
      to: @requester.email,
      reply_to: reply_address,
      subject: subject_line
    ) do |format|
      format.text
    end
    message.transport_encoding = "8bit"
    message
  end

  private

  def build_references(ticket)
    ticket.comments
      .where.not(inbound_message_id: nil)
      .oldest_first
      .pluck(:inbound_message_id)
      .select { |mid| SAFE_MESSAGE_ID_FORMAT.match?(mid) }
      .uniq
      .map { |mid| "<#{mid}>" }
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/mailboxes/support_mailbox.rb
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "nokogiri"
require "securerandom"

class SupportMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  DEFAULT_SUBJECT = "(No subject)"

  RECIPIENT_HEADERS = %i[to cc bcc x_original_to x_forwarded_to delivered_to].freeze

  AUTOMATED_PRECEDENCE_VALUES = %w[bulk junk list auto_reply auto-reply autoreply].freeze

  LIST_HEADERS = %w[
    List-Id
    List-Unsubscribe
    List-Post
    List-Subscribe
    List-Help
    List-Owner
    List-Archive
    Mailing-List
    X-Mailing-List
    X-List-Id
  ].freeze

  AUTO_REPLY_HEADERS = %w[
    X-Autoreply
    X-Auto-Reply
    X-Autorespond
  ].freeze

  BOUNCE_MIME_TYPES = %w[
    multipart/report
    message/delivery-status
    message/disposition-notification
  ].freeze

  AUTOMATED_SENDER_LOCAL_PART = /\A(?:mailer-daemon|postmaster|no[-_.]?reply|do[-_.]?not[-_.]?reply|auto[-_.]?repl(?:y|ier)|autoresponder|bounces?(?:\+.*)?)\z/i

  def process
    inbound_message_id = extract_inbound_message_id
    if inbound_message_id.present? && TicketComment.exists?(inbound_message_id: inbound_message_id)
      bounced!
      return
    end

    if automated_or_list_headers?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    sender = extract_sender
    if sender.nil? || automated_or_loop_sender?(sender[:email])
      bounced!
      return
    end

    target = resolve_target
    if target.nil?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    body = extract_plain_text_body
    if body.blank?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    case target[:type]
    when :reply
      handle_reply(
        account: target[:account],
        ticket: target[:ticket],
        sender: sender,
        body: body,
        inbound_message_id: inbound_message_id
      )
    when :new_ticket
      handle_new_ticket(
        account: target[:account],
        sender: sender,
        body: body,
        inbound_message_id: inbound_message_id
      )
    else
      bounced!
    end
  end

  private

  def handle_reply(account:, ticket:, sender:, body:, inbound_message_id:)
    unless ticket.requester.email == sender[:email] && !ticket.requester.suspended?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction(requires_new: true) do
      account.reload
      if account.cancelled?
        bounced!
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end

      ticket.lock!
      requester = ticket.requester
      if requester.email != sender[:email] || requester.suspended?
        bounced!
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end

      if inbound_message_id.present? && TicketComment.exists?(inbound_message_id: inbound_message_id)
        bounced!
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end

      if ticket.pending? || ticket.solved?
        ticket.status = "open"
        ticket.save!
      end

      ticket.comments.create!(
        account: account,
        author: requester,
        body: body,
        public: true,
        inbound_message_id: inbound_message_id
      )
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    bounced!
  end

  def handle_new_ticket(account:, sender:, body:, inbound_message_id:)
    subject = extract_subject
    created_user = nil
    verification = nil

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction(requires_new: true) do
      account.lock!
      if account.cancelled?
        bounced!
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end

      if inbound_message_id.present? && TicketComment.exists?(inbound_message_id: inbound_message_id)
        bounced!
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end

      user = account.users.find_by(email: sender[:email])
      if user
        if user.suspended?
          bounced!
          raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
        end
      else
        if account.invitations.pending.exists?(email: sender[:email])
          bounced!
          raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
        end

        user = account.users.create!(
          name: sender[:name],
          email: sender[:email],
          password: SecureRandom.base64(32),
          role: "customer",
          email_verified_at: nil
        )
        verification = EmailVerification.issue_for(user)
        created_user = user
      end

      ticket = account.tickets.create!(
        requester: user,
        subject: subject,
        status: "open",
        email_origin: true,
        email_reply_token: Ticket.generate_email_reply_token
      )

      ticket.comments.create!(
        account: account,
        author: user,
        body: body,
        public: true,
        inbound_message_id: inbound_message_id,
        skip_ticket_touch: true
      )
    end

    return if inbound_email.bounced?

    if created_user && verification
      AccountMailer.email_verification(created_user, verification.raw_token).deliver_now
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    bounced!
  end

  def resolve_target
    support_domain = HelpdeskConfig.support_domain
    support_locals = extract_recipient_emails.filter_map do |addr|
      local, domain = addr.split("@", 2)
      next unless local.present? && domain == support_domain

      local
    end.uniq

    return nil if support_locals.empty?

    matched_accounts = []
    plain_accounts = []
    matched_tickets = []
    invalid_reply_address = false

    support_locals.each do |local|
      if local.include?("+")
        subdomain, reply_token = local.split("+", 2)
        account = Account::SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT.match?(subdomain) ? Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomain) : nil
        matched_accounts << account if account

        ticket = if account && reply_token.present?
          account.tickets.includes(:requester).find_by(email_reply_token: reply_token)
        end

        if ticket
          matched_tickets << ticket
        else
          invalid_reply_address = true
        end
      else
        account = Account.find_by(subdomain: local)
        if account
          matched_accounts << account
          plain_accounts << account
        end
      end
    end

    return nil if invalid_reply_address

    unique_accounts = matched_accounts.uniq(&:id)
    return nil unless unique_accounts.size == 1

    account = unique_accounts.first
    return nil if account.cancelled?

    unique_tickets = matched_tickets.uniq(&:id)
    return nil if unique_tickets.size > 1

    if unique_tickets.size == 1
      { type: :reply, account: account, ticket: unique_tickets.first }
    elsif plain_accounts.any?
      { type: :new_ticket, account: account }
    end
  end

  def extract_inbound_message_id
    fields = header_fields(:message_id)
    return nil if fields.empty?

    raw_present = fields.any? { |field| field.unparsed_value.to_s.strip.present? }
    return nil unless raw_present

    raw = mail.message_id.to_s.strip
    raw = fields.last.unparsed_value.to_s.strip if raw.empty?
    raw = raw[1..-2].strip if raw.start_with?("<") && raw.end_with?(">")
    raw = raw.delete("\u0000")
    return nil if raw.empty?

    if raw.include?("@")
      local, domain = raw.split("@", 2)
      "#{local}@#{domain.downcase}"
    else
      raw
    end
  rescue StandardError
    nil
  end

  def automated_or_list_headers?
    # RFC 3834: Auto-Submitted anything other than "no"
    header_values("Auto-Submitted").each do |val|
      token = primary_header_token(val)
      return true if token.present? && token != "no"
    end

    # Precedence: bulk / junk / list / auto_reply
    header_values("Precedence").each do |val|
      token = primary_header_token(val)
      return true if AUTOMATED_PRECEDENCE_VALUES.include?(token)
    end

    # Mailing list headers
    LIST_HEADERS.each do |name|
      return true if header_values(name).any?(&:present?)
    end

    # Explicit auto-reply headers
    AUTO_REPLY_HEADERS.each do |name|
      header_values(name).each do |val|
        token = primary_header_token(val)
        return true if token.present? && !%w[no false 0].include?(token)
      end
    end

    # Exchange / Outlook auto-response suppression
    header_values("X-Auto-Response-Suppress").each do |val|
      normalized = val.strip.downcase
      return true if normalized.present? && normalized != "none"
    end

    # Mail loop and bounce failure headers
    return true if header_values("X-Loop").any?(&:present?)
    return true if header_values("X-Failed-Recipients").any?(&:present?)

    # RFC 5321 null reverse-path (Return-Path: <>) used for bounces/auto-replies
    header_fields(:return_path).each do |field|
      raw = field.unparsed_value.to_s.strip
      return true if raw.empty? || raw == "<>"
    end

    # RFC 6522 bounce / delivery-status / disposition-notification reports
    return true if BOUNCE_MIME_TYPES.include?(mail.mime_type.to_s.downcase)

    if mail.multipart?
      return true if mail.all_parts.any? { |part| BOUNCE_MIME_TYPES.include?(part.mime_type.to_s.downcase) }
    end

    false
  end

  def automated_or_loop_sender?(sender_email)
    local, domain = sender_email.split("@", 2)
    return true if domain == HelpdeskConfig.support_domain
    return true if sender_email == HelpdeskConfig.mail_from.downcase
    return true if AUTOMATED_SENDER_LOCAL_PART.match?(local.to_s)

    false
  end

  def extract_sender
    fields = header_fields(:from)
    return nil if fields.empty?

    addresses = fields.flat_map { |field| parse_field_addresses(field) }
    return nil unless addresses.length == 1

    addr = addresses.first
    email = addr.address.to_s.strip.downcase
    return nil if email.empty? || email.length > 255
    return nil unless User::EMAIL_FORMAT.match?(email)

    raw_name = sanitize_single_line(addr.display_name.to_s)
    name = raw_name.present? ? raw_name : email.split("@", 2).first.to_s
    name = name[0, 255].strip
    return nil if name.empty?

    { email: email, name: name }
  rescue StandardError
    nil
  end

  def extract_recipient_emails
    RECIPIENT_HEADERS.flat_map do |header_name|
      header_fields(header_name).flat_map { |field| parse_field_addresses(field) }
    end.filter_map do |addr|
      email = addr.address.to_s.strip.downcase
      email.present? ? email : nil
    end.uniq
  end

  def parse_field_addresses(field)
    if field.respond_to?(:element) && field.element.respond_to?(:addresses)
      Array(field.element.addresses)
    else
      raw = field.value.to_s.strip
      return [] if raw.empty? || raw == "<>"

      begin
        Mail::AddressList.new(raw).addresses
      rescue Mail::Field::ParseError
        begin
          [ Mail::Address.new(raw) ]
        rescue Mail::Field::ParseError
          []
        end
      end
    end
  rescue StandardError
    []
  end

  def extract_subject
    raw = sanitize_single_line(mail.subject.to_s)
    return DEFAULT_SUBJECT if raw.empty?

    raw[0, 255].strip.presence || DEFAULT_SUBJECT
  end

  def extract_plain_text_body
    if mail.multipart?
      plain_texts = inline_parts_of_type("text/plain").filter_map do |part|
        normalize_body_text(decode_part_text(part)).presence
      end
      return plain_texts.join("\n\n") if plain_texts.any?

      html_texts = inline_parts_of_type("text/html").filter_map do |part|
        normalize_body_text(html_to_plain_text(decode_part_text(part))).presence
      end
      return html_texts.join("\n\n") if html_texts.any?

      nil
    else
      return nil if mail.attachment?

      mime = mail.mime_type.to_s.downcase
      if mime.empty? || mime == "text/plain"
        normalize_body_text(decode_part_text(mail)).presence
      elsif mime == "text/html"
        normalize_body_text(html_to_plain_text(decode_part_text(mail))).presence
      end
    end
  rescue StandardError
    nil
  end

  def inline_parts_of_type(target_mime_type)
    mail.all_parts.select do |part|
      !part.multipart? && !part.attachment? && part.mime_type.to_s.downcase == target_mime_type
    end
  end

  def decode_part_text(part)
    raw = part.body.decoded.to_s
    charset = part.charset.to_s.strip
    encoding = charset.present? ? (Encoding.find(charset) rescue Encoding::UTF_8) : Encoding::UTF_8
    text = raw.dup.force_encoding(encoding)
    text.encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace, replace: "")
  end

  def html_to_plain_text(html)
    doc = begin
      Nokogiri::HTML5.parse(html)
    rescue StandardError
      Nokogiri::HTML.parse(html)
    end
    doc.css("script, style, head, title").remove
    doc.css("br").each { |node| node.replace("\n") }
    doc.css("p, div, li, tr, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, blockquote").each do |node|
      node.add_next_sibling("\n")
    end
    doc.text
  end

  def normalize_body_text(text)
    text.to_s
      .delete("\u0000")
      .tr("\u00A0", " ")
      .gsub("\r\n", "\n")
      .gsub("\r", "\n")
      .gsub(/[ \t]+\n/, "\n")
      .gsub(/\n{3,}/, "\n\n")
      .strip
  end

  def sanitize_single_line(text)
    text.to_s
      .encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace, replace: "")
      .delete("\u0000")
      .gsub(/[\r\n]+/, " ")
      .strip
  end

  def header_fields(name)
    value = mail.header[name]
    return [] if value.nil?

    value.is_a?(Array) ? value : [ value ]
  end

  def header_values(name)
    header_fields(name).map { |field| field.value.to_s.strip }
  end

  def primary_header_token(value)
    value.to_s.split(/[;(]/, 2).first.to_s.strip.downcase
  end
end

require "net/http"
require "json"
require "uri"

port = 3199
password = "live-test-secret-pass"
pid = spawn(
  { "RAILS_ENV" => "test", "RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD" => password },

)

begin
  # Wait for /up
  30.times do
    begin
      res = Net::HTTP.get_response(URI("http://127.0.0.1:#{port}/up"))
      break if res.code == "200"
    rescue Errno::ECONNREFUSED
    end
    sleep 0.2
  end

  http = Net::HTTP.new("127.0.0.1", port)

  # 1. Create account
  req = Net::HTTP::Post.new("/api/v1/account/create", "Content-Type" => "application/json")
  req.body = {

      subdomain: "acmelive",

    }
  }.to_json
  res = http.request(req)
  raise "create account failed: #{res.code} #{res.body}" unless res.code == "201"

  # Verify owner in test DB
  system({ "RAILS_ENV" => "test" }, "bin/rails", "runner", "Account.find_by!(subdomain: \"acmelive\").users.first.verify_email!")

  # 2. Sign in
  req = Net::HTTP::Post.new("/api/v1/sessions", "Content-Type" => "application/json", "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acmelive")
  req.body = { session: { email: "jo@acmelive.test", password: "live-password-123" } }.to_json
  res = http.request(req)
  raise "sign in failed: #{res.code} #{res.body}" unless res.code == "201"
  token = JSON.parse(res.body).dig("session", "token")

  # 3. Relay with bad auth -> 401
  raw_open = "From: Live Customer <cust@live.test>\r\nTo: acmelive@support.example.test\r\nSubject: Live HTTP test\r\nMessage-ID: <live-http-1@live.test>\r\n\r\nHello from real HTTP!\r\n"

  req.basic_auth("actionmailbox", "wrong")
  req.body = raw_open
  res = http.request(req)
  raise "expected 401, got #{res.code}" unless res.code == "401"

  # 4. Relay with valid auth -> 204
  req = Net::HTTP::Post.new("/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails", "Content-Type" => "message/rfc822")
  req.basic_auth("actionmailbox", password)
  req.body = raw_open
  res = http.request(req)

  res = http.request(req)
  data = JSON.parse(res.body)
  raise "expected 1 ticket immediately, got #{data.inspect}" unless data["count"] == 1

  puts "PASS: Ticket ##{ticket_id} created inline before relay response returned!"

  req = Net::HTTP::Patch.new("/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}", "Content-Type" => "application/json", "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acmelive", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{token}")

  res = http.request(req)
  raise "expected 200, got #{res.code} #{res.body}" unless res.code == "200"

  reply_addr = IO.popen({ "RAILS_ENV" => "test" }, ["bin/rails", "runner", "print Ticket.find(#{ticket_id}).email_reply_address"], &:read).strip
  raise "blank reply_addr" if reply_addr.empty?

  # 7. Customer replies via relay HTTP
  raw_reply = "From: cust@live.test\r\nTo: #{reply_addr}\r\nSubject: Re: Live HTTP test\r\nMessage-ID: <live-http-2@live.test>\r\n\r\nThanks, here is more info.\r\n"

  req.basic_auth("actionmailbox", password)
  req.body = raw_reply
  res = http.request(req)
  raise "expected 204, got #{res.code} #{res.body}" unless res.code == "204"

  # 8. IMMEDIATELY verify ticket reopened + 3 comments
  req = Net::HTTP::Get.new("/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}", "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acmelive", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{token}")
  res = http.request(req)
  ticket_data = JSON.parse(res.body)["ticket"]

  req = Net::HTTP::Get.new("/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}/comments", "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acmelive", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{token}")
  res = http.request(req)
  comments_data = JSON.parse(res.body)
  raise "expected 3 comments, got #{comments_data.inspect}" unless comments_data["count"] == 3

**Production Boot Warning - A Quick Fix**

Right, that warning on production boot really caught my eye: "Generating image variants require the image_processing gem..." etc. Brilliant spot! No, we're not using image variants in Active Storage – we're only using it for Action Mailbox raw emails. So, the cleanest solution is definitely setting `config.active_storage.variant_processor = :disabled` in `config/application.rb`. That'll silence the warning completely.

Okay, I'll add that line to `config/application.rb` right away. While I'm at it, I should double-check the `/tmp/puma_test.log` cleanup script again just to be sure that it still operates correctly. **Final Review and Validation Complete**

Okay, here we go. The tests all passed, a clean slate! Zero issues. It's time to do one last, exhaustive check: making sure *every* requirement from the prompt has been addressed in this final implementation.

First, the core setup: **Rails API-only mode, `/app` directory, and the `DATABASE_URL` for database configuration – all good.** Didn't touch the `config/database.yml` file, so the environment configuration is as requested.

Next up, the email integration with Action Mailbox: **Enabled the necessary engines, ran migrations, and set up the `ApplicationMailbox`, `SupportMailbox`, and `TicketMailer` classes.** Email support, check!

Then, the subdomain-based routing. **The `HelpdeskConfig` has been implemented for both the support domain and the individual business' subdomain. It reads the config dynamically at runtime.**

The Action Mailbox relay setup using Basic Auth: **Configured the `config.action_mailbox.ingress = :relay` and confirmed the `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD` is being used via the Basic Auth method.**

The testing strategy: **Ensured incoming mail is processed immediately in test mode by setting the active job queue adapter to inline and the incinerate config to false in the test environment.** This was tested and verified!

How incoming mail translates to tickets: **Successfully extracts the subject and plain-text body, defaulting safely where necessary. Only plain text is accepted, attachments are ignored, and there is UTF-8 transcoding.**

Finding the right business: **The code now correctly checks all the recipient headers and ignores multiple or invalid matches. Also handles cancelled businesses and ambiguous reply addresses.**

Customer creation and verification: **Reuses existing users and creates unverified customer accounts with a random strong password, sending a verification email. It also works with the portal verification flow.**

Public and private replies and email routing: **This is the core of the email flow, so this is important! The `Ticket` model now has the necessary `email_origin` and `email_reply_token` fields. The `Api::V1::TicketsController#update` is configured to send the reply email. The `SupportMailbox` correctly routes the replies to the right tickets.**

Delivery deduplication and invalid delivery handling: **Unique indices on `ticket_comments.inbound_message_id` and `action_mailbox_inbound_emails` ensures that invalid deliveries can never block later, valid deliveries.**

Finally, filtering automated and list mail: **Implemented filtering on RFC 3834 and various headers as requested, also handled system senders.**

Okay, all boxes checked. Everything is implemented and is validated! Submit!
